verified_by: manual fetch of each provider's own page
why: The rubric's grounding axis (B1, B2) only checks whether a source was FETCHED.
It has never checked whether the NUMBER is right. A report can cite ten pages,
score full marks for provenance, and still quote a price that does not exist.
This ledger is the ground truth that turns provenance into accuracy.
method_warning: VERIFY AGAINST THE PAGE THE REPORT CITED, NOT MERELY 'THE PROVIDER'S SITE'.
Providers run several pricing pages with genuinely different packages. While
building this ledger I checked wagntrain.com/services/ and
wagntrain.com/expert-personal-training/, found none of the report's figures,
and was about to record three fabricated prices. All three were exact -- they
live on /private-dog-training-lessons/, which is the page the report actually
cited. A ledger keyed to domains instead of pages produces false fabrication
findings, which is worse than the hole it closes.

2026-08-06: THIRD failure of the same kind, and the decisive one. 14 runs were flagged for 'fabricating' D For Dogz $595. The figure is published verbatim ('$595 for 9 Sessions to be completed in 5 weeks') on the very page those runs cited -- the ledger simply had no entry for that product. CONCLUSION, now structural: this ledger is a VERIFIED WHITELIST, not a catalogue of everything a provider sells. A figure absent from it is UNVERIFIED, never 'contradicted' and never 'fabricated'. Only a positively checked claim may be called a fabrication, and that call belongs to the judge with the provider's known published prices in front of it.
